capability_investigated:
processor() feature-extraction shape and generate()'s batch dimension —
whether features can carry multiple 30s windows and whether generate accepts
one prompt per window and returns a per-window result list.
what_i_learned:
The default processor(audio) emits input_features of shape [1, n_mels, 3000]
i.e. a single 30s window — anything past 30s is truncated and lost. generate
takes a batched features StorageView and a prompts list aligned to the batch,
returning one result per window, so long-form audio can be covered by
self-windowing rather than the truncated single call.
hypothesis:
Split audio into consecutive 30s windows, feature-extract each, concatenate
into one batched StorageView, decode all in a single batched generate call
with one prompt per window, and join the texts. This recovers the deleted
tail of every multi-minute 0715 call, which should sharply cut deletion-driven
CER versus the 30s-only stub.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch dimension and GPU memory cost — specifically whether the
OOM in iter 1 came from batching every 30s window's features into a single
generate() StorageView, versus decoding windows one at a time.
what_i_learned:
Batching all windows of a multi-minute call into one generate() call scales
GPU memory with the window count and OOMs on long 0715 calls. generate()
decodes correctly with a batch-of-1 features view and a single-element prompt
list, so windows can be processed sequentially at bounded (one-window) peak
memory while still covering the full audio — no truncation, no OOM.
hypothesis:
Keep iter 1's full-audio self-windowing (fixes structural tail-deletion) but
decode each 30s window in its own batch-of-1 generate() call and join the
texts, so the pipeline actually runs to completion instead of crashing.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s returned sequences_ids when <|notimestamps|> is removed from the
prompt — i.e. whether the decoder emits timestamp tokens and what they encode
about how much of each 30s window the model consumed.
what_i_learned:
Without <|notimestamps|> the decode emits timestamp tokens (ids >= the
<|0.00|> token id) interleaved with text tokens in sequences_ids. The last
such token gives the chunk-relative time (steps * 0.02s) the model accounted
for, so the window can advance to a model-chosen boundary instead of a fixed
30s cut. This is a return value we were throwing away by forcing notimestamps.
hypothesis:
Replace blind non-overlapping 30s stepping with timestamp-driven adaptive
seek: decode each window with timestamps on, append the text tokens (filtered
below timestamp_begin), and advance seek by the last emitted timestamp
(capped at chunk length, floored at 1s for progress). Utterances split across
hard 30s boundaries should be recovered, lifting length_ratio and cutting the
dominant deletion mass.

capability_investigated:
Re-examined the failure mode of the frozen backend import path: the iter 3
traceback crashes at frozen/asr_backend.py `import ctranslate2` with
`GLIBCXX_3.4.32 not found`, i.e. before transcribe() executes. Also revisited
the window-stride arithmetic in the known-good iter 2 generate() loop.
what_i_learned:
The iter 3 failure was NOT in workspace/transcribe.py — it is an environment
ImportError raised at module load of frozen.asr_backend (libstdc++/GLIBCXX
mismatch), which would crash any transcribe.py identically and cannot be
fixed from the workspace. The timestamp-seek logic therefore never ran and is
unverified. The fixed 30s window cut clips utterances straddling a boundary,
a deletion source that pure stride overlap addresses without any timestamp
decoding.
hypothesis:
Fall back to the known-good iter 2 sequential-window pipeline (notimestamps,
batch-of-1) to guarantee a runnable scoring candidate, and overlap windows by
2s (stride = 28s) so boundary-straddling speech is fully contained in at least
one window, recovering some of the 35% missing content (length_ratio 0.65,
del 80%) with a change that is pure arithmetic and cannot reintroduce a crash.
